risks.note: Fluctuations in key raw materials, crude oil derivatives, utilities and energy costs may impact production costs and operating margins; sustained inflationary pressure could hit profitability if increases cannot be passed on to customers. The MD&A ties material costs directly to brent crude movement, and management separately flags the risk of profitability impact in commodity-driven businesses.
risks.risk: Raw material and energy price volatility, tied to crude-oil derivatives

risks.note: Changes in global trade policies, tariffs, duties and geopolitical developments affect exports and supply chains. This was not theoretical in FY 2025-26: US tariffs of 50% seriously dented profitability, and the US-Israel-Iran war disrupted the final quarter through a cooking-gas shortage that triggered mass worker migration and a breakdown in PP polymer supply chains core to the floor covering business, forcing machine shutdowns despite healthy demand. Mitigation is diversifying export markets to reduce dependence on specific geographies and optimising FTA utilisation.
risks.risk: Trade policy, tariff and geopolitical exposure on a business where exports are 45.42% of turnover

risks.note: Risk of under-utilisation due to demand fluctuations, changing market dynamics and competitive pressures - structurally material because the Company has just commissioned floor covering capacity and fixed assets including CWIP have risen. Mitigation is expanding the customer base, differentiated products, manufacturing flexibility through product and capacity realignment, and strategic outsourcing and job work to improve asset utilisation.

Risk of delayed product development, unsuccessful product launches or quality-related issues affecting growth and profitability. Structural for AYM because growth depends on a qualification-led model where specialised yarns are co-developed with single customers and must clear technical approvals before scaling.

currentContext.expansion: The Company fully commissioned its expansion in flooring yarns during FY 2025-26, and the MD and CEO states the capacity has been taken up by new customers and programmes; the MD&A notes that this commissioning of Floor Covering capacity together with planned expansion is expected to enhance operating leverage, improve capacity utilisation and support long-term revenue growth. In the Industrial Yarns business, after three years of effort the Company achieved export-grade technical specifications on nylon technical yarn on a line it assembled itself at a third of the investment of standard lines available in the market, which management says allows roughly 3X the asset turns some competitors achieve in this product and opens more lucrative export markets. Average speed in technical yarn was raised by 25% during the year, with the gains expected to flow through in FY 2026-27. The Company also converted and commissioned another line by exiting a further commodity product, leaving 2 commodity products in the textiles business which it hopes to exit by converting or replacing the last 3 remaining lines by FY 2027-28, concluding an 11-year product-mix overhaul begun in 2016. Investment continued in nylon capacity and in the introduction of polyester and recycled polyester yarns for automotive applications. Plant-level investment during the year included energy-conservation equipment of Rs. 438 Lakhs at the Silvassa plant and Rs. 29.5 Lakhs at the Palghar plant, augmentation of solar power generation capacity, increased biomass-based fuel use for steam generation, and technology absorption spending on boiler feed water treatment systems, energy-efficient compressed air systems, cooling tower upgrades, high-efficiency utility pumps and an automated weighing system. Enterprise risk mitigation includes investing in capacity debottlenecking and infrastructure upgrades to improve productivity. The MD&A states that depreciation is expected to increase in the coming year on account of the committed capex plan.

- Shift the improvement focus from the revenue line to the expense line: deeper vendor development, project management and cost optimisation in secondary costs such as masterbatch, spin oils, freight and B-class capex items
- Plant speed optimisation - repeat in Flooring yarn and textiles the speed playbook proved in technical yarn over the last 12 months, where …

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

hero.oneLiner: AYM Syntex Limited is an Indian man-made-fibre yarn manufacturer that has shifted its portfolio from commodity yarns towards specialised, application-led products for textile, floor covering, automotive and industrial end-uses, with exports contributing 45.42% of its business in FY 2025-26.
